title: There's not a single image-gen or music-gen asset in this game. AI wrote the code that made everything.
author: Appropriate_Dot1219
selftext:
There's not a single asset in this game that came from an image generator or a music generator. AI wrote the code, and the code made everything: the 3D models, the UI, the sound, the music, the levels, and the store art.

Aussie Pop is a free mobile tower-defense / popping game. You place koalas, kangaroos, wombats and cockatoos to defend the pantry from snack thieves, across 100 levels, with upgrades like Turbo, Freeze and Boom.

The whole game is in C#: combat rules, map, shop, ads and in-app purchases. It has about 270 code tests, plus about 40 tests that actually play the game with drags and taps.

The characters (koala, kangaroo, wombat, cockatoo and the thieves) are sculpted by a Python script that generates the models. Nobody ever opened Blender. The buttons, panels and icons are drawn in code at runtime. The sound effects and both tunes are synthesized note-by-note by a Python script.

Two of the levels were handmade. The other 98 came from a generator, and every level is validated by code players: a smart bot that has to 3-star it, and a random bot that must not win too often.

Screenshots, the icon, the banner and the trailer are all generated from the game itself with one command. The trailer was captured frame by frame while code plays a level.

I'd love to hear from anyone else who has tried to keep image and music generators out of the asset pipeline and do it all in code. What would you still refuse to hand off?

It's free on Google Play and the App Store:

[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.orenlevyapps.aussiepop](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.orenlevyapps.aussiepop)

[https://apps.apple.com/il/app/aussie-pop/id6836363721](https://apps.apple.com/il/app/aussie-pop/id6836363721)

comments.author: outminded
comments.body: If AI wrote it is still gen art. How do you think art was made?

replies.author: Appropriate_Dot1219
replies.body: That's a totally fair point, and thanks for raising it! You're right, it's still AI-made in the end. What I meant is the pipeline: no image or music model produced any pixels or audio. The AI wrote Python and C# that builds the meshes from simple shapes, draws the UI, and synthesizes the sound note by note. So every asset is reproducible from code, and I tweak one by editing a parameter instead of re-prompting. Different route, same AI help, and I appreciate you pushing on it.
